Subject: Northridge pilot: procurement timeline, stakeholder map, and SLA ask

Hi Priya / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and the things we committed to follow up on: 

1) Stakeholder map (who signs/offers):
   - Economic buyer: Tom Ellis (VP Product) — final budget sign-off
   - Procurement lead: Priya Shah — purchase order and contract intake
   - Security/infosec reviewer: Dinesh Kapoor — SOC2 & data residency questions

2) Timeline you shared: procurement kickoff next week, target PO by 2/15, pilot start window 3/1–3/15.

3) Outstanding asks from your side:
   - Completed procurement questionnaire (Priya said she’ll send)
   - SOC2 summary and retention/data-flow diagram from us
   - Confirmation on pilot SLAs and whether a limited SLA carveout is acceptable for a short-term pilot

Next steps (from Redwood side):
- I’ll attach a first-draft SOW for the pilot and a short SOC2 summary.
- Laura will coordinate enablement and the sample telemetry we’ll provide during pilot.
- If procurement requests an SLA reduction (e.g., lower uptime or rollback windows), we’ll need internal approval for any deviations.

Priya — thanks for promising the procurement questionnaire. Once we have that I’ll loop in our contracts team. If you can confirm preferred billing entity and any specific security questionnaires (SIG, MyVCI, etc.), that’ll speed things up.

Attachments: pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (draft), SOC2_summary_Redwood.pdf (summary)

Best,

- Procurement will need a standard PO and our legal team will want to redline the SOW. Timeline: procurement review week of 1/18, legal review week of 1/25 (target PO 2/15 is realistic).
- Security asked for the SOC2 summary and an answer on whether Redwood will accept a 30-day data-retention requirement for pilot logs. Dinesh (cc) will own that conversation.

Subject: Fwd: Northridge pilot: procurement timeline, stakeholder map, and SLA ask

Folks — forwarding Priya’s questionnaire and ask about a pilot SLA concession. Quick internal take and recommended route: 

1) Discount/credits ask: procurement is requesting a 25% credit if downtime exceeds 48 cumulative hours in first 60 days. Our standard pilot discounts are approved at up to 20% without senior approval. Anything over that should go to Aditya/Revenue Ops. We should propose a 20% pilot credit cap and tie any additional credit to documented operational failures (incidents with RCA).

2) SLA carveout: I don’t recommend removing contractual uptime entirely for the pilot. Proposal: provide a limited operational SLA with explicit exclusions for known onboarding risks, and offer a 60-day pilot SLA with a target availability (non-contractual) plus a 30-day remediation plan. If procurement insists on the 60-day contractual carveout, we should treat that as a security exception that needs sign-off from Legal & Security.

3) Security evidence: SOC2 summary should be fine as a first pass, but Dinesh may want the full report or a bridge letter. Marcus — please ask Dinesh which specific SIG questions he needs answered so we can prioritize.

4) Next steps: Marcus to propose a final pilot clause (I can draft), then route to Aditya for discount approval and to Contracts for a controlled redline.

Attaching internal template: pilot_approval_form.xlsx (please fill in expected pilot MRR, expected GA timeline, and proposed credits).

Thanks,
Laura
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-13T15:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Northridge pilot: procurement timeline, stakeholder map, and SLA ask

Thanks for the context — I approve a constrained approach for this pilot: 

- Pilot credit: approve up to 20% one-time credit for the pilot if downtime > 48 cumulative hours during the first 60 days. Any additional credit must be escalated to REVOPS and approved in writing.
- SLA carveout: do not agree to a full contractual SLA removal. We will offer a time-limited operational SLA for the pilot (documented target availability and a clear remediation plan). If Legal requires a carveout clause we’ll add explicit scope boundaries and limit the period to the pilot only; Legal must accept the clause.
- Security requests: approve sharing SOC2_summary_Redwood.pdf and an engineer-run session with Dinesh to answer SIG questions. Marcus — set that up and ask Dinesh to send the list of required SIG modules.

Action items: Marcus to: 1) send revised pilot clause & SOW to Priya by 1/14, 2) create HubSpot deal RDW-2347 and tag Access:Contracts, RevOps, Security, 3) schedule 30-min technical call between Redwood infra lead and Dinesh (put in Doodle).

I’ll also notify Revenue Ops to standby for any discount escalation.
